notes:
K8Secret 0.6.9 — errors that say what actually went wrong.

When K8Secret refuses a connection, it now tells you why it refused, instead of leaving you with a message that points at your cluster.

Two of them were genuinely misleading. Rejecting a server's certificate showed the single word "cancelled" — as though you had done something. Failing to present a client certificate showed a TLS error, which reads as the cluster being broken when it is answering perfectly well. Both now name the step that failed: which host, which setting in your kubeconfig to look at, and what macOS said about it.

If you are the person who wrote in about a cluster that connects on one Mac and not another, this is the release to try — and if it still fails, the error itself should now tell us both which of the two causes it is.
